thread:
idan: Quick one Landing CPH at 00:30, 7h layover before morning train. Any secret nap spots or late food that arent a souvlaki pit?
soph: The far end of Terminal 3 (near gates E) is surprisingly quiet at night. Lots of benches with armrests removed = slightly better for lying down.
max: Theres a small pay-per-shower place near the arrivals hall last time I checked. Otherwise use lounge day passes if you can snag one.
portbot: CPH tip: many charging stations are USB-C now. Map: https://www.cph.dk/en/airport/shops-and-services/charging-points
nicole: For snacks, try the bakery kiosks inside security 1 they do good sandwiches and yoghurt. Avoid anything super oily if you want to sleep.
idan: Luggage? lockers at the airport or haul to central station?
soph: Lockers are limited but convenient. If you have time, central station has more options and often cheaper for long stashes.
max: Sleep kit: eye mask, light hoodie (planes/terminals get cold), earplugs. Also set 2 alarms 15 min apart.
nicole: Power: get a 20k mAh battery (under 100Wh) and a short cable. USB-C to USB-C is best for modern outlets.
idan: Any couch/sofa spots that arent super bright? Lights wake me up.
soph: The small family rooms near gate clusters are dimmer and less trafficked. Not private but quieter.
max: If you want privacy and will pay, the airport hotel has day rooms. For cheap privacy, look for a quiet corner and a scarf as a blanket.
portbot: Reminder: If youre transferring between Schengen/non-Schengen, allow extra time to re-clear security.
nicole: If anyone has a spare lounge guest pass (or pastry) I will trade a sticker sheet :grin:
idan: I will bring stickers. DM me if you need a checklist before you go.
